notes:
CRM notes / workshop summary:
- Business context: global three-tier logistics operator; AI assistants for dispatch and carrier support; heavy real-time requirements for driver-chat and ETA adjustments.
- Current infra: internal GPU pool (NVIDIA A40/A100 mix) used for training; ops team reluctant to operate inference 24/7 at scale. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable ops + cost.
- Use-case profile and targets (from workshop):
  * Primary workload: dispatch-assistant chat + task reranking. Mix = 60% chat, 30% rerank, 10% embeddings/cosine lookups.
  * Baseline steady-state QPS: 12 req/s (business-hours), average request = 420 tokens (prompt+expected generation) => steady tokens/sec ≈ 5040 t/s.
  * Peak traffic: burst to 45 req/s for 6-8 minutes every ~15 minutes during peak dispatch windows; peak avg tokens/request increases to ~650 => peak tokens/sec ≈ 29,250 t/s (short bursts).
  * Latency SLOs: target p50 ~55ms, p95 <= 200ms for chat flows; reranking p95 <= 150ms. Cost sensitivity medium-high; prefer reserved capacity but want burst/burst-scaling policy.
- Sizing assumptions used in workshop:
  * Model family: open LLM ~7B-13B (quantized), expected per-GPU sustained throughput for average prompt with caching ~6k-8k tokens/sec on A100-80GB.
  * Steady-state capacity math: 5040 t/s / 7000 t/s ≈ 0.72 GPUs => recommend reserving minimum 2 GPUs for headroom + model variants.
  * Burst capacity plan: ability to scale to 6-8 GPUs to cover 29k t/s bursts; propose reserved pool 4 GPUs with autoscale burst to 8 for 10-15 min windows.
  * Recommendation: initial reserved pool = 4x A100-80GB (dedicated) with configured burst allowance to 8 for short windows; revisit after 2-week POC.
- SLA / contract items flagged by procurement and legal:
  * Required uptime target: 99.95% with clear definition for maintenance windows and regional failover. Procurement pushing for 99.99% for critical flows.
  * Throughput guarantees: need contractual wording for sustained throughput at reserved pool size (e.g., 4 GPUs => sustained X tokens/sec) and guaranteed burst behavior (time-limited).
  * Credits & remedies: accrue credits for SLA breaches; procurement requests faster incident response (<1h for Sev1).
  * Security: must support SSO (SAML), audit log retention 1 year, ability to integrate with KMS for key control and meet SOC2 requirements. Data residency: US-only for driver PII.
- POC acceptance criteria:
  * Sustained latency: p95 chat <=200ms under steady-state workload for 48 hours.
  * Burst handling: no more than 5% error rate during scheduled peak bursts and p95 degradation <2x baseline.
  * Cost telemetry: per-token cost report and token-level billing for 4 week run.
- Comments from technical stakeholders (quoted / paraphrased):
  * "We need real numbers, not best-case. If burst kills our SLAs we can't move forward." – VP Eng, Maria Chen.
  * "Key ask: show how Redwood will route to fallback lightweight model if primary is overloaded; we can't have dispatch stalled." – Head of SRE.
- Action items (owner):
  * SE Priya: update GPU sizing sheet with observed POC numbers and recommended reserved/burst config (due 2026-03-03).
  * AE Jordan: update pricing worksheet and deliver term sheet with proposed 99.95% SLA + credit schedule (due 2026-03-05).
  * Legal/Procurement: provide SLA redlines by 2026-03-09.
- Risks / notes:
  * Cold KV cache increases latency significantly for some rerank flows; suggested caching warmers and prefetch policies in Redwood Optimize.
  * Network peering for VPC required; current internal network team timing is main procurement blocker.
- Internal scoring: 8/10 (high fit) — strong need for dedicated predictable inference but procurement SLA and VPC are blockers.
